newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Tunisian tourism firm sells 15.76 pct of capital.
newsitem.headline: Tunisian tourism firm sells 15.76 pct of capital.

text.p: Tunisia's tourism firm Societe de Tourisme et de Congres is offering 15.76 percent of capital, or 208,000 shares to local and foreign investors at $3.3 million, a spokeswoman said on Thursday.

"Societe de Tourisme et de Congres is offering 208,000 shares, or 15.76 percent of its capital, to local and foreign investors at 17 dinars per share," a spokeswoman at Tunis-based Sofiges stockbroker told Reuters.
The offered shares, which belong to the municipality of Tunis, will be ceded on the stock exchange as part of the state policy to withdraw from the competitive sectors, the spokeswoman said.
No closing date for the offer was set, she added.

Established in 1981 in Tunis, Societe de Tourisme et de Congres has a capital of 1.32 million shares equivalent to 13.2 million dinars. It registered a turnover of 14.8 million dinars and a net profit of 1.6 million dinars in 1996, Sofiges said.
In the previous year it posted a net profit of 1.0 million dinars, it added.

Tunisia plans to privatise some 63 firms and stakes in large companies such as national airline Tunis Air and oil distribution group Societe Nationale de Distribution des Petroles by end-1997, a senior official said earlier.
One of the main tourism destinations in North Africa, Tunisia showed 1.4 billion dinars in tourism receipts in 1996, up from 1.3 billion dinars in 1995, officials said.
